judged_text: The findFirst-then-create sequence is not atomic, so two concurrent or retried webhook deliveries for the same userId+appSlug can both observe no existing credential and both take the create branch. Duplicate Credential rows accumulate for the same user and app (or the duplicate insert is rejected as a 500 if a unique index exists); subsequent syncs update whichever row findFirst returns first, leaving duplicates stale and credential resolution nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the code checks for an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }})` and then conditionally calls `prisma.credential.create(...)` if none is found. This check-then-act sequence is not atomic and is vulnerable to concurrent/retried webhook deliveries: two requests can both see no row and both attempt `create`, producing duplicate credential rows (if no unique constraint) or triggering an insertion failure (if a unique constraint exists). The finding accurately describes nondeterministic updates because subsequent syncs use `findFirst` and will update an arbitrary matching row.
